The smell of slow-cooked cabrito and smoked pulled pork filled Nuevo Laredo's stand at the Feria Tamaulipas 2026 this week, as the border city hosted the closing of the state fair's Gastronomic Showcase — and the crowds showed up.

According to El Reportero de Tamaulipas, more than 10,000 visitors passed through Nuevo Laredo's stand over five days, making it one of the most-visited spaces at the fair. The city government, working with the Sociedad Parrillera de Nuevo Laredo, served two specialties representing northern flavor: cabrito and lonches de pulled pork ahumado, offering fairgoers from Tamaulipas municipalities a taste of the border city's culinary identity.

The closing ceremony drew Mariana Álvarez Quero, the state subsecretary for small and medium business, who recognized Nuevo Laredo's gastronomic diversity and invited Tamaulipas families to visit the border city to experience its food, entertainment, and tourist attractions firsthand.

Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal highlighted the value of using state showcases to project Nuevo Laredo's strengths and to present the city's tourism, culture, and recreation projects — among them the Science and Technology Museum, which drew strong interest from visitors across Tamaulipas as a new option for family knowledge, innovation, and entertainment.

City officials said the fair presence is part of an effort to project an image of Nuevo Laredo beyond its commercial and border importance — its culture, traditions, gastronomy, and spaces for family gathering and tourism.

Sources:

  • El Reportero de Tamaulipas
  • Luis Valtierra Noticias
  • Nexus Tamaulipas

— Waldo Wolf, Nuevo Laredo Correspondent, Webb Watch 956
